Emma — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front so procurement can proceed: yes, billing is based on tokens for all three endpoints, but there are practical differences in counting and feature-costs that change the effective unit math. I attached the current hosted ratecard (redwood-hosted-ratecard-202611.pdf) and below is a concise mapping you can paste into your RFQ.

Quick mapping (pasteable):
- Chat Completions (chat endpoint): billed per 1K tokens; invoice shows combined prompt + output tokens. System and user messages are tokenized the same as prompt content. Function call payloads (args returned by model) are billed as output tokens. Streaming does not add extra billed tokens beyond generated tokens.
- Responses (unified responses endpoint): billed per 1K tokens as well. Responses treats the conversation as a single request with context tokens and generated tokens; however, it supports structured fields and tool-call metadata that can add overhead (metadata is tokenized and billed). Responses includes a small request-level processing fee for extremely high QPS (only applies at scale; visible as a separate line item on enterprise invoices).
- Legacy completions endpoints: billed per 1K input tokens + 1K output tokens historically; in practice this aligns to the above for our hosted models, but older integrations that do batch prompt concatenation can lead to higher prompt token counts.

Example (conservative): 300 token context + 800 token generated = 1,100 tokens -> billed as 1.1K tokens (rounded to 1K granularity on invoice lines). If function-calls return an extra 200 tokens, billable total becomes 1,300 tokens.

Discount guidance (baseline):
- Standard hosted list: see attached PDF.
- Typical committed pricing: 10% off for $50k+/month contracted, 15% for $150k+/month, 22% for $350k+/month ARR-style commit. These are baseline ranges and can be formalized in a term sheet.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want a worked example using the numbers in your RFQ.

Cheers,

Adding the appendix text below (copyable). I also included two worked examples using the RFQ volumes so procurement can see line-item math.

Appendix A — token mapping (copy into RFQ):
1) What counts as a token: all textual bytes sent to or generated by the model are tokenized (system instructions, user messages, assistant output, function call args). Non-text attachment references (e.g., image pointers) are not tokenized; however, if you include the OCRed text or raw HTML, that content is billed.
2) Streaming: streaming only changes delivery; tokens are billed the same as if the full response were returned in one chunk.
3) Function calls: the model's return payload (arguments) are billed as assistant output tokens. If you ask the model to serialize a large JSON payload, those tokens are billed.
4) Responses endpoint metadata: metadata fields (structured keys, tool output wrappers) are tokenized; plan on a small overhead for structured outputs (+~2-6% token overhead typical for JSON wrappers).

Worked example A — conversational customer chat (Neon estimate: 6M monthly generated tokens):
- Per interaction average: 280 prompt tokens (system + user history) + 720 generated = 1,000 tokens
- Monthly: 6M generated + 2.333M prompt = ~8.333M tokens total
- At list price (example): $0.40 / 1K tokens -> $3,333.20 / month
- At 15% committed discount -> $2,833.22 / month

Worked example B — nightly summary pipeline (Neon estimate: 2M generated tokens, heavy structured output):
- Per run average: 500 prompt tokens + 1,500 generated + ~100 tokens metadata = 2,100 tokens
- Monthly total: ~4.2M tokens
- At list price $0.40 / 1K tokens -> $1,680 / month
- At 15% discount -> $1,428 / month

Notes: numbers above use a placeholder list rate for illustrative math. The ratecard PDF has exact list rates per model family and per 1K tokens. For Responses endpoint, include a 2-6% metadata overhead on structured outputs in your calculations.

If you want, I can produce a CSV with those line items at list and 10/15/22% discount tiers for the RFQ.
